# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/mirui/0.39.0/src/mirui/lib.rs.html

# mirui/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! mirui — a `no_std`, ECS-driven UI framework for embedded, desktop,
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//! and (planned) WebAssembly. Renders with 24.8 fixed-point subpixel
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! precision on a software rasterizer designed for MCUs without an FPU;
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! optionally runs on top of SDL2 (CPU or hardware-accelerated) on
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! desktop.
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//!
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! # Quick Start
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! ```toml
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! [dependencies]
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! mirui = { version = "0.39", features = ["sdl"] }
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! ```
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//!
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! The snippet below builds against mirui's default features and is
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! verified by `cargo test --doc`. Swap `FramebufSurface` for
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! `mirui::surface::sdl::SdlSurface::new("hello", 480, 320)` (with the
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! `sdl` feature) to run on a desktop window instead of into a
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! user-supplied flush callback.
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! ```no_run
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! use mirui::prelude::*;
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! use mirui::surface::framebuf::FramebufSurface;
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! use mirui::render::texture::ColorFormat;
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! use mirui::types::Rect;
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! let backend = FramebufSurface::with_format(
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//!     480, 320, ColorFormat::RGBA8888,
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!     |_bytes: &[u8], _area: &Rect| { /* push to your display */ },
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! );
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! let mut app = App::new(backend);
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! app.with_default_widgets().with_default_systems();
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! let root = app.spawn_root().id();
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! ui! {
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!     :(
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!         parent: root
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!         world: &mut app.world
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!     :)
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!     header (
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!         bg_color: ColorToken::Primary,
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//!         text_color: ColorToken::OnPrimary,
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!         text: "Hello mirui!",
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!         border_radius: 8
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!     ) {}
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! };
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! app.run();
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! ```
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! # Other targets
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! mirui also runs bare-metal on RISC-V and ARM Cortex-M MCUs through
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! [`surface::framebuf::FramebufSurface`], and a Cargo workspace
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! template builds the same UI code on both desktop and embedded
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! targets unchanged. The full walkthrough — including ESP32-C3
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! wiring, the workspace layout, and a recipe for adding new target
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! crates — lives in [`docs/quickstart.md`][quickstart].
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! [quickstart]: https://github.com/W-Mai/mirui/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//!
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! # Module map
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! - [`app`]: the [`App`][app::App] entry point, the [`Plugin`][app::plugin::Plugin]
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!   trait, and bundled plugins.
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! - [`core`]: cross-cutting infrastructure — cache, resource, the
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!   [`reactive`][core::reactive] runtime (Signal / Computed / Effect),
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!   perf tracing, timer.
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! - [`ecs`]: World, Entity, Component, Resource, Query, System, SystemScheduler.
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! - [`ui`]: widget tree primitives (Style, View, Theme, Dirty),
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//!   [`ui::layout`] (flexbox + absolute positioning), and [`ui::widgets`]
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!   (built-in widget instances — buttons, sliders, lazy lists, effects).
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! - [`render`]: software rasterizer, paths, textures, draw commands, font,
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!   and concrete [`render::backends`] (sw / sdl_gpu / wgpu / web_canvas).
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! - [`input`]: input dispatch, gestures, hit-testing, focus,
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!   and visual [`input::feedback`] overlays.
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! - [`surface`]: backend trait + bundled SDL2 / framebuffer / SDL_GPU /
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//!   wgpu / web_canvas / Linux / NuttX implementations.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! - [`anim`]: easing, springs, motion components.
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! - [`types`]: Color / Dimension / Fixed / Point / Rect / Transform / Viewport.
[82](https://docs.rs#82)

# FramebufSurface in mirui::surface::framebuf - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/mirui/0.39.0/mirui/surface/framebuf/struct.FramebufSurface.html

## Expand description

Owns a physical-pixel-sized byte buffer and calls the user flush
callback each frame. `width` / `height` are the **physical**
framebuffer size; HiDPI is opt-in via `with_scale`.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

    physical_h: [u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html),
    scale: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/types/fixed/struct.Fixed.html),
    flush_cb: F,
) -> Self

Construct a backend that renders into a `physical_w × physical_h`
byte buffer but reports `(physical / scale)` as the logical
screen size — user code then writes its layout against the
logical dims and the scale is applied by the render pipeline.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/mirui/surface/framebuf.rs.html#42-64)

`display_info()`; backends that store physical dims directly
should override to skip the multiply-and-round.**physical-pixel**region of the backing surface.

`App` is responsible for converting a logical dirty rect to physical
before calling this; driver-side code treats `area` as raw device
coordinates / buffer offsets.[Source](https://docs.rs/src/mirui/surface/framebuf.rs.html#88-90)
